input.quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation.
input.rationale: Garman owns all IP in the Work, including the Improvements and the Schedule "D" Modifications we pay for (§13), while our only right is a non-transferable, non-exclusive, location-limited licence (§2) that is expressly not sublicensable (§3(c)) and endures only while fees are paid and the Agreement is not terminated (§17(a)). That fails the fallback licence-back position on its material terms: the licence is neither perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide nor royalty-free (extra fees apply beyond Authorized Locations), and there is no right to modify or sublicense for our business. There is also no provision limiting Garman's use of our converted data (§4(b)) to providing the services. We therefore target the fallback: Garman retains ownership of the Work (already met at §13), but our licence is conformed and Garman's use of our data is confined to service delivery.

proposal.summary: Convert the §2 grant into a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Work, conform the §3(c) sublicence bar, and limit Garman's use of our data to providing the services.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Garman keeps ownership of the Work, but we need the fallback licence position: a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free right to use, modify and sublicense the Work for our business, so we have conformed the sublicence restriction in Section 3(c) and the location/extra-fee limits that contradict it. We have also confirmed that any licence to Garman in our data is limited to processing it solely to provide the services.
